title: repair two broken workflow step paths, guard them with a test, and file what the exclusions really hide
action: Close the CI loop honestly. Validation deleted this cell's headline job — read why. THE EXCLUSIONS ARE NOT REMOVED IN THIS SLICE. The earlier draft removed all four on the strength of a local pass; validation measured all four passing on this Linux machine and pointed out that they were excluded precisely BECAUSE Windows differs, so a Linux pass is definitionally not evidence about them. Worse, two of the four are documented as having causes this slice does not touch: windows.yml:90-92 lists for test_bee_cli.mjs 'linked-worktree reverse gitdir pointer mismatch on C:\ paths, plus doctor-wording/recovery-window/registry-example failures' — four classes, one addressed — and test_cells.mjs:1634-1639 skips its write-failure simulation on euid 0, which never fires on win32 where geteuid is undefined, while chmod there does not prevent directory entry creation. Removing those exclusions would convert a documented red into a surprise red. WHAT THIS CELL DOES INSTEAD, three parts. (1) Fix BOTH broken workflow step paths: windows.yml:114 runs node scripts/test_portable_paths.mjs and :117 runs node scripts/test_config_validate.mjs; both files live under scripts/tests/. Neither step can succeed today, and both have been masked by the job failing earlier. (2) Add a test that validates workflow step script paths — nothing in the repo does this today, which is why two broken steps sat unnoticed. It must parse the workflow files, extract every `node <path>` invocation from run steps, and assert each path exists; prove it discriminates by pointing one step at a nonexistent file in a fixture and watching it fail. (3) File one backlog row per remaining Windows cause with what is actually known: test_bee_cli's three non-path classes named individually, test_cells' permission-model difference with its line anchor, and test_bee_write_guard_hook plus test_misc recorded as having NO diagnosed cause — that absence is itself the finding, since attributing them to path identity was assertion. Update windows.yml's comment block to say what is now true: the exclusions stand, one contributing cause has been fixed, each remaining cause is filed, and removal is gated on a Windows run showing the suite green. HONEST VERIFICATION LIMIT: this machine is not Windows. Local green proves no POSIX regression and proves the workflow paths resolve; it proves nothing about Windows behaviour. Write that sentence in the report and do not write one that reads as though Windows was verified here.
